additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

patient_info.stressor: Jaime’s small finance office underwent a major restructuring, and despite being only 19 she was asked to help rebuild budget templates, explain changes bilingually, and absorb late-night reporting deadlines while still taking college classes. During the following 4 months, her habit of keeping snacks nearby during spreadsheet work escalated into repeated private eating episodes after long meetings, when she would consume amounts far beyond a normal meal despite not feeling hungry and then feel uncomfortably full. She felt especially ashamed because she was known as organized, energetic, and health-conscious, so she avoided inviting friends over for cooking nights and hid the extent of the eating from coworkers and family. Jaime eventually sought care herself through a student counseling referral after journaling about feeling unable to control these episodes and realizing the pattern had become recurrent rather than an occasional response to stress.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: What made me come in is that after work or class I’ll sit down with my laptop and end up eating a whole takeout meal plus chips, sweets, and whatever snacks are in my desk drawer, way more than I ever planned or than I’d eat around anyone else.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like I’m watching myself keep reaching for the next thing even while I’m thinking, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish and you’re not even enjoying this anymore.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: By the end I’m so full that my stomach feels tight under my work pants and I have to just sit there for a while because moving around or bending over makes me feel sick.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: A lot of the time it starts right after I’ve already had dinner, when I’m not physically hungry at all but I still go back to the kitchen or order more food because my mind feels restless.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ve been waiting until my roommate is out or my family has gone to bed, because I’m embarrassed for anyone to see how much I can eat after acting so put-together and health-conscious during the day.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: When I looked back through my journal and food delivery charges, these episodes have been happening most weeks since the restructuring started, usually more than once a week and not just here and there.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve been avoiding friends and family plans like cooking nights because I’m worried they’ll notice how much I’ve been eating privately, so I’ve been more isolated outside work and school.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 4 months, ever since the office restructuring and late-night reporting deadlines started.
